title: Quincy, Washington shows what’s possible when you build datacenters with communities, and grow together over time.
summary: Quincy, Washington shows what’s possible when you build datacenters with communities, and grow together over time. | 60 comments on LinkedIn
body_markdown: [Brad Smith](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bradsmi?trk=public_post_comment-text) &[Satya Nadella](https://www.linkedin.com/in/satyanadella?trk=public_post_comment-text) , a big part of datacenter unpopularity, in my view, comes from the fact that they’re often hidden behind barbed-wire fences and remain almost completely opaque to the public. What if we flipped that model? A datacenter could also be a Museum of Data — part critical infrastructure, part science museum — where people can safely explore how computation, AI, energy, cooling, data governance and digital infrastructure actually work. That transparency becomes even more interesting when combined with[Inter Dimensional Computation | IDC™](https://se.linkedin.com/showcase/inter-dimensional-computation/?trk=public_post_comment-text) and PRIVACY-as-PRESENCE. Instead of data only flowing inward and value flowing upward, IDC can support a reciprocal model where value generated through computation can flow back toward the people and communities participating in the system — through mechanisms such as tokens, subscription kickbacks, access, shared benefits and eventually broader participation in the economic value created. Closed infrastructure creates suspicion. Visible infrastructure can create literacy, trust and participation. Maybe the datacenter of the future shouldn’t just compute for society. Maybe society should be able to walk inside and understand it. More:[YourFinestOut.com](http://yourfinestout.com/?trk=public_post_comment-text)
